apps.description: Private, read-only Uptime Kuma client for Android: monitor your self-hosted servers' status, uptime, response times & certificates on the go. FOSS, GPLv3, Material You, no ads or tracking.
apps.releaseNotes:
### Fixed

- **A monitor shows the address that matches its type.** Uptime Kuma's own form leaves 'https://' in the URL field of every monitor it creates, whatever the type, and the app showed that URL whenever there was one. So a ping, DNS, port or push monitor showed 'https://', or a URL pointing somewhere else, under its name.
- **The list and the certificates tab now pick the address by type**: the URL for web checks (HTTP, keyword, JSON query, real browser, websocket upgrade), host:port for port, Steam, GameDig and MQTT checks, and the host for the rest. A push monitor with no host shows nothing. On the detail screen, the URL line only shows for web checks, and real-browser and websocket-upgrade monitors now show their type instead of a dash.

en.summary: Read-only viewer for your Uptime Kuma monitors. Private, no ads, no tracking.

Replied and forwarded marks

- A message you replied to or forwarded now shows it, in the message list and in the message header. The marks come from the server (IMAP '\Answered' and '$Forwarded', JMAP '$answered' and '$forwarded'), so a reply sent from another client shows too. Messages already on the phone get their marks on the next sync, within the sync window; older ones get theirs as you scroll to them (#259).
- When a reply, reply-all, forward or forward as attachment is sent, Sterna sets the mark on the original, on the account it was read in. This also covers a reply sent offline, scheduled, or from a notification (#259).
- In the message list and in the header of a message that isn't encrypted, the mark shows as soon as the reply is in the outbox, so you see it during the undo de
